content.text:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `performance` (performance): Load the CPU like a busy mid-range phone, then scroll the screen and use its slowest action; the UI must never freeze.
Steps: [{"fault": "cpu_stress", "threads": 4}, {"scroll": "down"}, {"scroll": "up"}, {"tap": "product_1"}, {"settle": 8.0}]
Result: froze: 1 frozen frame(s) over 700 ms and 3 slow UI-thread frames (p99 53 ms): something blocks the main thread

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The row's clickable lambda calls Thread.sleep(1500) on the UI thread before invoking onProductClick (ShopScreen.kt:56). Compose dispatches the tap on the main thread, so every tap parks the thread for 1.5 s and the input event cannot finish. Under the cpu_stress fault the already-busy CPU makes the block longer and the main-thread frame exceeds 700 ms. The shop list has no reason to wait before navigating, and the detail screen already handles slow loading through its own ViewModel path (ProductRepository.byId, a 5 s delay, ProductRepository.kt:37).
Fix approach: Remove the Thread.sleep from the clickable lambda so it only calls onProductClick(product.id) right away. Any intended latency belongs off the main thread, in the ViewModel or repository (suspend calls in a coroutine scope). The detail screen should show its own loading state while byId runs. Keep the click handler non-blocking so input dispatch returns immediately.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/ShopScreen.kt:56 - .clickable { Thread.sleep(1500); onProductClick(product.id) } blocks the main thread on every row tap; Perfetto: long main-thread slice 'dispatchInputEvent MotionEvent UP ... deliverInputEvent' 1501 ms, of which sleeping/blocked 1500 ms, running 1 ms. This matches the 1500 ms sleep inside the click lambda; Perfetto: main thread sleeping/blocked 95% of the trace, and 1 frozen frame over 700 ms, which is the tap on product_1; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/data/ProductRepository.kt:37 - byId is a suspend function with delay(5_000), so detail loading is already meant to be async and off the click path

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/ShopScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add a Compose UI test in src/androidTest, ShopScreenTapTest, that renders ShopScreen with a recording onProductClick and taps the node tagged product_1. It asserts that onProductClick(1) is called and that the tap-to-callback latency is under 100 ms, with no Thread.sleep in the path. Before the fix the callback arrives after about 1500 ms and the test fails. After the fix it passes. This needs the Android runtime (Compose semantics and input), so an instrumented test is the right choice.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart

import androidx.compose.ui.test.ExperimentalTestApi
import androidx.compose.ui.test.hasTestTag
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onNodeWithTag
import androidx.compose.ui.test.performClick
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.ShopScreen
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test

class ShopScreenTapTest {

    @get:Rule
    val composeRule = createComposeRule()

    @OptIn(ExperimentalTestApi::class)
    @Test
    fun tapOnProductInvokesCallbackWithoutBlocking() {
        val clicked = mutableListOf<Int>()
        composeRule.setContent { ShopScreen(onProductClick = { clicked += it }) }
        composeRule.waitUntilExactlyOneExists(hasTestTag("product_1"), 5_000)

        val start = System.nanoTime()
        composeRule.onNodeWithTag("product_1").performClick()
        val elapsedMs = (System.nanoTime() - start) / 1_000_000

        assertEquals(listOf(1), clicked)
        assertTrue("tap-to-callback took $elapsedMs ms", elapsedMs < 100)
    }
}
